facts.text: Drivers use dashboard navigation screens in newer cars, while many older vehicles still rely on road signs.
A driver checks tire pressure at a service station before a long trip.
Many families choose a sport utility vehicle or minivan for errands and vacations.
A teenager practices parallel parking before taking a driving test.
Parents wait in a line of cars outside the elementary school at dismissal.
A yellow school bus stops along rural roads to collect students in the morning.
Some school districts install cameras on buses to monitor passing vehicles.
Drivers encounter temporary lane closures near highway resurfacing crews.
A road crew paints fresh lane markings on the highway after repairs.
Some towns add marked bicycle lanes along busier streets.
Children wear helmets while riding bicycles around the neighborhood.
A commuter secures a bicycle to a rack outside the library.
Some commuters arrange carpools to share fuel and parking expenses.
Drivers use electronic toll passes on highways that charge tolls.
A traveler prints a boarding pass at home before heading to the airport.
Airline passengers remove shoes at security checkpoints before boarding domestic flights.
A passenger train stops at a regional station where travelers wait with luggage.
A small-town bus route may run only a few times each weekday.
A family checks highway rest areas before leaving on a long drive.
A driver pulls into a gas station and pays at the pump with a card.
Some motorists compare fuel economy when shopping for a used car.
Hybrid cars appear in parking lots alongside conventional gasoline vehicles.
Electric car charging stations begin appearing at some public parking areas.
A delivery van stops along Main Street to drop parcels at local businesses.
Ride-hailing services become an option in some larger nearby cities before reaching many smaller towns.
A parent checks that a young child is buckled into an appropriate car seat.
